about.7: 🔒 Ranking can't be bought with money
about.9: Jjin Matjip is a verified restaurant map service that removes the hassle of hopping between map apps and blogs to filter out sponsored reviews.
about.10: Map services just show every restaurant in a radius, without telling you which ones are actually good. Blog/SNS reviews are hard to trust since sponsored/ad content is mixed in. In the end, the burden remained on users to hop between platforms comparing reviews one by one.
about.11: To solve this, Jjin Matjip takes the approach of keeping the familiar map as-is while layering a 'verification layer' on top of it.
about.12: Using the Google Places API, AI analyzes review credibility and shows only places that pass verification. You can check exactly why a store passed on the Verification Methodology page.
about.13: We support integration with Kakao Map, Naver Map, and Google Maps, so you can keep using whichever map platform you're used to.
about.14: "The only thing owners pay for is the 'store management pass.' This payment only grants the right to directly register menu/photos/description — it has no effect whatsoever on map/search ranking."
about.15: Through the monthly subscription, AI learns your preferences (diet, category, revisit patterns, etc.) and prioritizes personalized restaurant recommendations.
about.16: To let you quickly find 'restaurants you can trust' with Jjin Matjip alone, without hopping between platforms to compare reviews. We currently serve mainly the Hwaseong area, but nationwide service is our goal.

verification.390: Jjin Matjip doesn't have humans review registered stores one by one. Instead, it automatically goes through the steps below using data from the three map providers and AI, and keeps the result (reason for approval/rejection) as-is. This page exists to explain those steps transparently. It's not a perfect filter — please also read the "Limitations" section below.
verification.391: The registered name and coordinates are searched on Naver, Kakao, and Google simultaneously. If none of them find it, it's left as "pending," and it's cross-checked once more for the same name within 50m of the registered coordinates, to rescue new openings that don't show up in search yet.
verification.392: Checks whether the location found on the map service and the location registered by the user are within 500m. If it's too far, it's judged as "the name matches, but this doesn't look like the actual registered location" and rejected.
verification.393: If Naver reviews exist, it is rejected when fewer than 50% of rated reviews are 4 stars or higher. This criterion doesn't apply to brand-new stores with no reviews at all.
verification.394: We show the AI the original Naver review text and photos and have it judge two things.
verification.395: In this process, a credibility score (0-100) and situational tags (solo dining, date, gathering, family, late night, parking available, good value, great atmosphere) are also extracted and shown on the map card.
verification.396: The 'store management pass' owners pay for is just a feature that lets them directly register/edit menu, photos, and description — it has absolutely no effect on map/search ranking or the verification badge. Keeping the two signals "paid" and "actually verified" separate is Jjin Matjip's core principle.
verification.399: Since this is an AI judgment, there may be false positives/negatives (wrong approvals/rejections). Please report any you find.
verification.400: If a store has actually closed but its information remains on a map service, Jjin Matjip may not filter it out immediately either. Please refer to the "recently checked" badge above for how fresh the information is.
verification.401: Credibility is currently analyzed based on Naver reviews. Including Kakao and Google reviews in the analysis is a goal for the next stage.
